evidence.quote: MongoDB Atlas for Government is a fully-managed cloud database for the U.S. government (federal agencies and state, local, and education (SLED) entities).
Much of the information and many of the procedures in the [Atlas documentation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/) hold true for AtlasGov, but there are key differences.
Review the following sections to understand the restrictions and limitations of the MongoDB Atlas for Government environment.

edits.old: An IsDown reproduction of MongoDB’s October 23, 2025 federated-login incident says a small number of federated users could be unable to sign in to Atlas or the Support Portal. It says Atlas for Government users could log in at cloud.mongodbgov.com; existing logins and cluster health were unaffected. This is a historical login incident, not evidence of Azure Government hosting. (low confidence)
edits.new: MongoDB's status page reports an October 23, 2025 incident, 'MongoDB Atlas and Support Portal: Browser-initiated Federated logins fail'. It affected a small number of federated users, who could not log in to Atlas or the Support portal. The same issue affected Atlas for Government, whose users could log in at cloud.mongodbgov.com. Existing logins and cluster health were unaffected. Sources: https://status.mongodb.com/incidents/bk7zs5yl85kg

evidence.quote: This affects a small number of federated users. Affected users who attempt to login via their federation will not to be able to login to Atlas or the Support portal
The same issue affects Atlas for Government, so users there could go to cloud.mongodbgov.com to login.
Existing logins are unaffected. Cluster health is unaffected.

A fix has been deployed and we are monitoring the results.

Posted Oct 23, 2025 - 22:44 UTC

edits.rationale: The incident content is confirmed on MongoDB's own status page. The IsDown URL returned HTTP 403 and could not be pinned, so the claim is re-sourced to the primary page. The status page says the same issue affected Atlas for Government, not that those users were unaffected. The claim's 'could log in at cloud.mongodbgov.com' wording is therefore misleading as written. The 'not evidence of Azure Government hosting' remark is an editorial inference and is left out.

edits.old: Do not infer AtlasGov Azure Government availability from commercial Azure support or generic government branding: Microsoft documents separate service-availability checks, while AtlasGov explicitly excludes Azure and the commercial Atlas changelog contains an unexplained Azure-government backup entry. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)
edits.new: Do not infer AtlasGov Azure Government availability from commercial Azure support or generic government branding. Microsoft's Azure Government documentation points to its 'Products available by region' page for service availability. The AtlasGov API documentation lists Azure as unavailable for all API resources. The commercial Atlas changelog contains an entry enabling cloud backup for clusters deployed in the Microsoft Azure government environment. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/government/api.md ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-government/compare-azure-government-global-azure ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/release-notes/changelog.md

edits.old: In the AtlasGov documentation snapshots dated October 14, 2026, Azure is explicitly unavailable for all API resources. The supported-provider page lists AWS GovCloud, selected AWS commercial regions, and GCP Assured Workloads, with no Azure Government offering. This establishes the documented AtlasGov support boundary; it does not resolve the conflicting general Atlas changelog entry. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
edits.new: The AtlasGov API documentation lists Azure as unavailable for all API resources. The AtlasGov supported cloud providers and regions page lists AWS GovCloud, four AWS FedRAMP Moderate standard regions, and GCP Assured Workloads in all standard US regions, with no Azure offering. This establishes the documented AtlasGov support boundary. It does not resolve the commercial Atlas changelog entry about cloud backup in the Microsoft Azure government environment. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/government/api.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/government/overview/supported-regions.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/release-notes/changelog.md
